report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of 4 of checks.py, covering not_substituted, unresolved_first_party_imports, imports_resolve, and BASELINE tuple.
risks: unresolved_first_party_imports | medium | Claim about MEASURED date (2026-07-30) is uncheckable; no external data provided.
unresolved_first_party_imports | medium | Claim about three specific imports (daedalus.linting, ShiftManager, daedalus.wiki_vault) is uncheckable; no test or external data provided.
BASELINE | low | Comment 'Cheapest first' is an opinion; order is load-bearing only in one direction as stated, but not verifiable without callers.

handoff.purpose: Implements not_substituted, unresolved_first_party_imports, imports_resolve, and defines BASELINE tuple.

symbols.name: not_substituted
symbols.note: Returns empty string if survival rate >= policy.min_symbol_survival; otherwise returns a message about suspected content substitution.

symbols.name: unresolved_first_party_imports
symbols.note: Returns list of first-party imports that cannot be resolved statically in the given repo tree.

symbols.name: imports_resolve
symbols.note: Returns empty string if all first-party imports resolve; otherwise returns a message listing unresolved imports.

symbols.name: BASELINE
symbols.note: Tuple of check functions in order: not_truncated, no_elision, parses, not_substituted, imports_resolve.

claims.text: The original parsed and the replacement does not. Whatever this is, it is not an improvement, and letting it land would break an import for every consumer of the module.
claims.why: The code returns the message 'rewrite does not parse as Python while the original did' when before is not None and after is None, consistent with the claim.

claims.text: Twenty agents wrote test modules against source files they were given, and three of seven imported things that do not exist: ``daedalus.linting`` (it is ``daedalus.gui.lint``), ``ShiftManager`` from ``daedalus.shift`` (the class is ``Shift``), and ``daedalus.wiki_vault`` (it is ``daedalus.wiki.vault``). All three are valid Python, so a syntax gate passes them, and all three reported ``status: done``.
claims.why: No external data or test results are provided in this chunk to verify the historical measurement.

claims.text: The check is STATIC on purpose. Importing the file to find out whether its imports resolve would execute module-level code from an untrusted lane -- the one thing this repository refuses to do to decide whether to trust something.
claims.why: The function uses ast.parse and checks file paths statically without importing modules, consistent with the claim.

claims.text: Conservative by construction, because a false refusal costs real work: only first-party roots are judged; a missing MODULE is reported, since that cannot be a re-export; a missing NAME is reported only when the module has no star-import and no module-level ``__getattr__``.
claims.why: The code filters by first-party roots, checks module existence via _module_path, and for names it skips opaque modules (star-import or __getattr__) via _exports.

claims.text: `from daedalus import shift` binds a SUBMODULE, which is perfectly valid and is named nowhere in the package's __init__.py. Measured: without this the check fired on 40 of 223 real files in this repo -- a false-positive rate that would have made the gate useless and, worse, trained everyone to ignore it.
claims.why: The code explicitly checks if the alias name is a submodule via _module_path(f"{node.module}.{alias.name}") and skips reporting if it exists, matching the claim.

claims.text: Checked for CREATED files too -- a brand-new test module against an invented API is exactly the failure this catches, and it has no original to compare against.
claims.why: The function does not check attempt.creating; it always runs unresolved_first_party_imports on the proposed content, regardless of creation status.

claims.text: Cheapest first. Order is load-bearing in one direction only -- the refusal a caller sees should be the most specific one available, and "does not parse" is more useful than "82% of definitions vanished" when both are true.
claims.why: The order in BASELINE places 'parses' before 'not_substituted', so if both triggers, the parse error will be reported first, matching the claim.

observations.what: not_substituted returns empty string if attempt.creating is True, skipping the check for new files.
not_substituted uses toplevel_defs which is not defined in this chunk; its behavior is assumed but not visible.
unresolved_first_party_imports references _module_path and _exports which are not defined in this chunk.
The docstring of unresolved_first_party_imports includes a MEASURED date (2026-07-30) and specific statistics that cannot be verified from this code alone.
imports_resolve uses attempt.proposed and attempt.repo_root; these attributes are assumed from WriteAttempt but not defined in this chunk.
BASELINE references not_truncated, no_elision, parses which are not defined in this chunk.
